summary: Lara Braitstein works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University, studying under Richard P. Hayes, and has taught Alnis Dickson.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Minnesota. He held teaching posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, Washington, and Langara College (attested 2005), and a research position at Chicago.

Lars Fogelin is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli, and held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo (~1971–1997), Heidelberg, and Bonn. He held a teaching post at the University of Oslo (attested 2002).

Lata S. Bapat is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She completed her PhD under M. P. Marathe at Savitribai Phule Pune University by 1985 and served there as a Research Associate in Buddhist Philosophy (attested 1989).

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ganden Shartse (Geshe Lharampa 1959) and Gyuto Monastery, served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (~1976–1984), and was a Visiting Scholar at Virginia (~1976–1977).
Latika Lahiri (born 1923) is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University in 1958 and later held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 1986).

Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University, where Robert A. F. Thurman was her doctoral supervisor alongside numerous other teachers.

Lauran Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, a teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and a consultant/editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) was a Tibetologist and archaeologist. After medical studies at Glasgow (~1874–1878), he served in the Indian Medical Service/Army (~1880–1906) and became Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) studied at Trinity College, Oxford (~1888–1892), working in Japanology and Sinology. He held long-term posts at the British Museum (~1893–1933) and Harvard University (~1933–1934), and taught Arthur Waley.

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jianmin Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Sangharakshita, and others around 1959–1963. He served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978 and taught Ayya Khema.

Laurie L. Patton (born 1961) is an Indologist who earned her PhD at Chicago (~1983–1991). She held posts at Emory (~1996–2011), Duke (~2011–2015), and served as President of Middlebury College (2015–2024) and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2024).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who served as a Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a Professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and served as a professor at the University of Oxford until 1918.

Lawrence William Nelson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied across several institutions, earning a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012).

Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati (~1916–1923) and served as Director of Prajna Pathashala from approximately 1935 to 1994.

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson and Ngawang Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2011, he was attested as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University and Research Associate in Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.
